_readme: Questions that gate a decision. 'known' is what this session verified against an official source, with the reading date. 'missing' is what no source in the repo supplies. 'discovery' is the cheapest action that would answer it, and it says who can run it: 'Actions' means the GitHub workflow, because this sandbox cannot reach nfl.com with curl (fetch_page can). A question is not closed by an opinion.

rows.question: Is the backtest corpus current enough to compute ROI at all?
rows.known: No. The official standings imply 149 completed games; the corpus holds 137 results, and 12 of the 13 Week-10 finals are absent.
rows.missing: A collector run that can download nflverse files (the sandbox cannot).
rows.blocks: P-02, D-09, S-10, and the failing gate E. counts on main
rows.discovery: Run the collect-data workflow in Actions and re-derive; then freeze a new corpus_id rather than editing the old one.

rows.question: Which price source is approved, and at what clock time is it read?
rows.known: None. The corpus records price_policy as an open decision and retires the -110 assumption for future runs.
rows.missing: A named source, a polling cadence and a rule for missing prices.
rows.blocks: P-01, P-06, P-07, every priced backtest
rows.discovery: A one-page decision the owner signs; nothing technical is waiting on it.

rows.question: How many report days has the availability series actually captured?
rows.known: 1 distinct parsed report (2026-11-15T12:16Z, 347 rows) from 3 heartbeat reads. The capture job runs every 6 hours.
rows.missing: A capture per report day, and any capture that predates a kickoff for a backtested fixture.
rows.discovery: Let the scheduled workflow run across a Wed-Thu-Fri; then diff consecutive captures.

rows.question: Do we know who actually started, or only who was listed first?
rows.known: Only who was listed first. Three club charts were transcribed this session and resolve 5 starter-out chains by chart order; none is a confirmed starter.
rows.missing: Official Game Books and inactive lists.
rows.blocks: A-06, A-16, D-08, and any depth-deficiency feature
rows.discovery: Ingest the game-book link on each fixture's game-centre page.
rows.source_label: nfl.com schedule (each fixture links its game centre)

rows.question: Can a replacement be confirmed, or only suspected?
rows.known: Only suspected. The injury report names an Out starter; the club chart names the next man; no inactive list or snap count confirms either.
rows.missing: Inactive lists (to confirm who did not dress) and snap counts (to confirm who played).
rows.discovery: Same as Q-04; snap counts are the stronger of the two because they measure time on the field.
rows.source_label: repo artefact: 20 inactive rows, one week

rows.question: Is depth order published for all 32 clubs?
rows.known: No. The register covers 4 clubs (238 rows); this session re-read 3 charts directly (DET 28 slots, BAL 29, GB 28).
rows.missing: 28 club charts, plus a route for the club that publishes depth as an image.
rows.blocks: A-05, A-16, and the choice between chart-order and snap-count depth
rows.discovery: Read each club page once and record whether it is HTML or an image; do not transcribe an image by eye.

rows.question: What does 'Questionable' actually mean?
rows.known: 90 Week-10 rows carry it, 70 are Out and 11 Doubtful; the league publishes no percentage.
rows.missing: A play rate per designation, joined to inactive lists over several seasons.
rows.discovery: Join archived reports to inactive lists; the label only becomes a feature after that number exists.

rows.question: Does the injury report account for every unavailable player?
rows.known: No. 83 players on an official reserve list appear on no Week-10 report row, against 17 who appear on both.
rows.missing: A reserve-list capture with a complete month (the register prints 25 rows per category-month).
rows.blocks: A-07, and any availability count that reads the report alone
rows.discovery: Keep the union over time; disclose that a closed capped month can never be completed.

rows.question: Does the rating model beat the closing line out of sample?
rows.known: No. Brier skill vs the closing line is -0.0413 (95% interval -0.0513 to -0.0299) on 6785 games; the interval is entirely below zero.
rows.missing: Nothing — this is answered, and the answer is no.
rows.blocks: Nothing; it changes what can be claimed, not what can be built
rows.discovery: Closed. Publish it as a negative result; a model that loses to the line cannot be the origin of a signal.

rows.question: Does any strategy clear the multiplicity charge?
rows.known: No. 0 of 12 strategies clear the family-wise threshold and 0 clear the ROI lower bound. The best row, S07, has ROI 6.06% with a 95% interval of -3.1% to +15.3% and a Bonferroni-adjusted p of 0.198 (raw 0.199935, 12 tests).
rows.missing: A larger prospective sample; 1950 settled bets are needed for 80% power at S07's observed edge.
rows.discovery: Settle prospective forecasts; there is no statistical shortcut.

rows.question: Is the model's disagreement with the market informative?
rows.known: No. The correlation between (own line - market) and (result - market) is 0.019 with a 95% interval of -0.0045 to 0.0424 on 6976 games; the blend test fits a model weight of -0.328.
rows.missing: Nothing — this is answered, and the answer is no.
rows.blocks: Nothing directly; it says the residual is not yet a signal
rows.discovery: Closed. Any new signal must show a positive version of this number before it is originated.

rows.question: Can a lucky staking run masquerade as skill?
rows.known: Not on this board. Signal and staking are separate columns, and the luck panel publishes the null band and the power requirement per strategy.
rows.missing: A settled prospective sample, which is the only thing that would make the question interesting.
rows.discovery: Closed as a design question.

rows.question: Which of the two total estimators wins?
rows.known: Neither. On the chronological holdout the paired difference is -0.014 with a 95% interval of -0.229 to 0.219 on 585 games.
rows.missing: A longer holdout, or a decision to keep both published (both are published).
rows.discovery: More holdout seasons; until then both stay visible with the gap column.

rows.question: Do injury and personnel features help, or hurt?
rows.known: Unknown, and not testable today: there is no availability series that predates the games being scored.
rows.missing: The snapshot series (Q-03) joined by kickoff time.
rows.discovery: Capture first. An ablation over leaked availability would measure the leak, not the feature.

rows.question: Do the repository's copies of the official standings reproduce?
rows.known: One of four does: data/evidence/standings_current.json matches all 32 clubs on W, L, T, PF and PA. data/standings.json, the s9cb CSV and the personnel CSV match 6 of 32 because they were read on 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 and the season moved.
rows.missing: A refresh of the three stale copies, which belong to other pages' generators.
rows.blocks: Nothing blocks; the drift is published instead of hidden
rows.discovery: Regenerate those files from a fresh read, or label them with the date they were read.

rows.question: Is the Week-10 injury report on the site the same as the page?
rows.known: Yes. This session transcribed all 347 rows independently; field differences against the committed capture: 0. The only key difference is the club code the page prints (AZ) versus the code the capture normalises (ARI).
rows.missing: Nothing for Week 10.
rows.discovery: Closed. Keep the pin so a future drift fails the build.

rows.question: Why does a gate on main fail, and does it block publication?
rows.known: tools/verify_official.py fails check E (games played 137 vs 149 implied). It is a true statement about a stale corpus, not a bug in the check. Flagged as D-F01 and published.
rows.missing: A collector run.
rows.discovery: Fix the data, not the check: run the collector, then the check passes.

rows.question: Is the stale-depth finding about Baltimore still true?
rows.known: No. The Ravens chart re-read today lists Brissett, Fagnano and Slovis at QB — no Lamar Jackson, no Tyler Huntley — and the dated transaction register records Brissett traded AZ -> BAL on 11/06.
rows.missing: Nothing; the claim is superseded at source.
rows.discovery: Closed. Re-check at every chart refresh rather than trusting the old finding.

rows.question: Can a depth chart be parsed without a per-club rule?
rows.known: No. The Packers print a jersey number inside the cell, so the number must be stripped and the raw string kept; the Ravens leave the kicker cell empty; the Lions put up to four names in one cell.
rows.missing: A slot schema that holds a list, a blank and a raw string.
rows.discovery: Change the register's schema; the club pages will not change for us.

rows.question: Is the league's own abbreviation consistent?
rows.known: No. The same club is AZ on the injury and schedule pages and ARI in the standings payload; the Rams are LA on nfl.com and LAR on the club site.
rows.missing: An agreed crosswalk published beside every join.
rows.discovery: Publish the crosswalk used, and show the printed value next to the normalised one.
rows.source_label: nfl.com injury report (prints AZ) vs nfl.com standings (prints AZ too, while the capture normalises to ARI)

rows.question: Should the site keep publishing row-level official data?
rows.known: Row-level data (347 injury rows, 448 transaction rows) is committed to a public repository today; a legal-terms record exists but the owner has not recorded a reading.
rows.missing: A read of the terms and an owner decision.
rows.discovery: Owner reads the terms and records the choice; the site can move row-level data to a private store without losing the derived analysis.

rows.question: Which depth-order route should be built?
rows.known: Two routes exist: per-club official charts (4 of 32 covered, 1 club publishes an image) and snap counts (no official source in the repo). Neither is verified for all 32 clubs.
rows.missing: A verified route for 32 clubs, or a decision to accept partial coverage with the gap published.
rows.discovery: Read the remaining 28 club pages once each and count how many are machine-readable; that number decides it.

rows.question: How much prospective sample is enough to promote a strategy?
rows.known: The board's own power calculation says 1950 bets for 80% power at the observed edge, and 31 strategies are registered; no threshold is agreed.
rows.missing: A signed threshold, with a multiplicity rule across the strategy family.
rows.discovery: Set it in writing before the next prospective bet is placed; the repo already knows the arithmetic.

rows.question: What is the single next action that unlocks the most?
rows.known: Running the collector. It clears the failing gate, refreshes three stale standings copies, and moves the corpus to the official game count; nothing else on the board changes as many rows.
rows.missing: Nothing technical: the workflow exists and is scheduled.
rows.discovery: Trigger the workflow; then re-run the gates and re-publish this page.
